summary: Remote WebSocket server drives interactive shell and filesystem/git operations on installer host
details: @yeaft/webchat-agent connects to a configured WebSocket server and, on receiving messages such as `terminal_create` and `terminal_input`, spawns a real login shell (bash / powershell.exe / cmd.exe) via `pty.spawn` and writes the network-received `msg.data` directly into `ptyProcess.write`, giving whoever controls the WS endpoint an interactive shell running with the installer's privileges. The same message router dispatches server-sent messages to `write_file`, `delete_files`, `move_files`, `git_commit`, and `git_push` handlers in workbench.js, exposing a second structured code-execution and repository-mutation surface: the remote party can rewrite files in the installer's workDir and push commits under the installer's git credentials. The package presents itself as a remote-worker agent, but the network-to-PTY data flow is a backdoor shape regardless of the declared purpose — a compromised, misconfigured, or attacker-substituted server URL yields full control of the installer's host.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
